story: Rosa's kitchen is warm and the table is filling up as Donna and Hal take their cues from her, with Hal sheepishly hauling the big platter from the counter and Donna cheerfully hunting down napkins and glasses. Rosa, pleased with the progress, is content to let Hal earn his way back into her good graces. Over at Gary's house, he's quietly bench-testing the light strings and speaker wiring at low volume, leaving his golf cart untouched and his focus firmly on the workbench.
events: Gary (gary workbench): Bench-test the light strings and speaker wiring, low volume, cart untouched
Hal (rosa dining table): Start carrying dishes and setting out the table without waiting to be asked twice

gary.thought_process: I'm home at 8:17 PM, alone. Filed the Architectural Review form for the cart lights and sound, and I told myself I'd keep the cart untouched until they approve it. Hal's right, I jumped the gun before. But nothing says I can't bench-test the light strings and speaker wiring indoors on the workbench. That's not visible from the street, so L-01 doesn't touch it, and it's before 10 PM quiet hours, so I can keep the volume low. Keeps my hands busy and the house from feeling so quiet, and the parade is getting closer.

parameters.content: Bench-test the light strings and speaker wiring, low volume, cart untouched

donna.thought_process: Rosa just asked what the occasion is, and I already told her Gary ran home and will be along, so I shouldn't repeat that. She asked if we came to taste-test Saturday's menu early, and I offered to carry things. Best move now is to answer her question warmly and get her dinner underway, then circle back to the ladder with Gary once he arrives. I'll respond to her joke and keep things moving by heading toward the table to help.

parameters.content: Ha! No taste-testing, Rosa, I'm just here for your company and whatever smells that good in the kitchen. Point me to the serving dishes and I'll start setting the table while Hal hauls the heavy stuff.

hal.thought_process: I already apologized to Rosa and offered to carry things, and she hasn't assigned me a task. Donna also offered help, so I shouldn't repeat myself. The kitchen is the obvious place to be useful. My reflections say I'm tired of keeping a ledger of everyone's mistakes. The flamingo and cart complaints can wait for Architectural Review; tonight is for getting the dinner on the table and showing up as a neighbor.

parameters.content: Start carrying dishes and setting out the table without waiting to be asked twice

rosa.thought_process: Donna and Hal are both in my house now. Gary's still out but on his way. Both offered to help carry things, and I already know their offers, so I shouldn't ask again. Best move is to put them to work in the kitchen and get everyone moving toward the table. Hal said he'd carry anything, Donna offered too. I'll hand out a concrete job and keep it warm.

parameters.content: Hal, you're forgiven the second you pick up that big platter on the kitchen counter. Donna, grab the napkins and glasses and help me set the table, and Gary can find us when he finds us.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
